goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3 — host format regex requires a TLD of `[a-z]{2,5}`, rejecting valid newer long TLDs like .technology, .international, and .museum, and also rejects IP-address hosts, preventing admins from adding legitimate hosts

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new model `EmbeddableHost` adds `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`, which hard-limits the TLD to 2–5 letters and requires a DNS-style hostname. That will reject legitimate modern longer gTLDs (e.g. `.technology`, `.international`) and also reject IP-literal hosts (e.g. `192.0.2.10`). Since this validation runs on create/update in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, admins would be prevented from adding such hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:27 — host values from site_settings are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), which can corrupt or fail the migration on apostrophes/special characters and is injection-prone; use parameterized/sanitized inserts

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from `val.split("\n")` (stored site_settings value), any single quote or other special characters in `h` will break the SQL (or alter it), and it is not escaped/sanitized. Using bound parameters or quoting via the connection would avoid both migration failures and SQL-injection-style risks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11 — `record_for_host` uses `where(...).first` with no ordering; combined with the missing uniqueness validation on host, multiple rows can match and the category chosen for imported topics (topic_embed.rb:38) is nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without any `ORDER BY` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and the migration creates no unique index on `embeddable_hosts.host`, so multiple rows for the same host can exist. In that case, `.first` may return any matching row depending on DB query plan/physical order, making the selected category for TopicEmbed.import (`eh.try(:category_id)` in app/models/topic_embed.rb) potentially inconsistent when duplicates exist. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13 — the 'raises an error with a missing host' test no longer stubs a referer/host context distinctly; with zero EmbeddableHost records and no referer stub it can pass for the wrong reason (missing referer), masking regressions in the host check

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test "raises an error with a missing host" previously forced the "no allowed hosts" condition by setting SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil. After the diff, that setup is removed and the test simply calls `get :comments` without stubbing `request.referer`. With the new implementation (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`), a nil referer will make `host_allowed?` return false (URI(nil) -> rescue -> nil), so the request fails due to missing/invalid referer regardless of whether EmbeddableHost records exist. This means the test no longer specifically verifies the "no allowed hosts configured" path and can pass for the wrong reason, weakening coverage and potentially masking regressions in host-check logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:13 — `update` is a no-op that just re-serializes the model, and the client (admin-embedding.js.es6 saveChanges()) calls `embedding.update({})` against it with no error handling (no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`), making the PUT endpoint misleading dead API surface

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` (line ~13) does not persist or modify anything; it just re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct via `render_serialized`. On the client, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload and does not attach any `.then`/`.catch(popupAjaxError)` handling. So the PUT endpoint and the save action form a misleading, effectively no-op “save” path that can fail silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs:1 — `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` renders the table header even when the hydrated list is an empty array (empty arrays are truthy in Ember's if), showing a header with no rows instead of hiding the table

adjudication.rationale: In Ember templates, the built-in `{{#if}}` helper does not behave like plain JavaScript truthiness for arrays; it uses Ember’s “emptiness” semantics (via `isEmpty`/`Ember.isEmpty`). An empty `Array`/`Ember.Array`/`DS.ManyArray` is treated as empty and thus the `if` block will *not* render when there are zero `embeddable_hosts`. Therefore the claim that the header will render for an empty array is not a verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:45 — `delete()`'s `destroyRecord()` promise has no rejection handler (no `popupAjaxError`), so a failed delete fails silently; `cancel()` for an unsaved record also silently discards without user feedback on failure

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which does). If the DELETE request fails, the rejection is unhandled and the user gets no feedback, which is a real defect introduced by this code. The second claim about `cancel()` for a new/unsaved record “failing” is not really applicable because that path only removes the record from the client-side list and makes no request that could fail in the same way.
